slides.title: Reasoning under uncertainty starts with a probability model
Evidence is observed; target variables are hidden; a model connects them
Random variables name uncertain aspects; distributions assign probability to their values
A valid joint distribution covers every complete assignment
A joint model makes the probability of any event computable
Select the rows that satisfy the event, then add each row once
A marginal distribution collapses a joint table by addition
Conditioning restricts the population; it does not imply time or causation
Fix the evidence value, then normalize every compatible row
The selected mass is exactly the probability of the evidence
Selection preserves ratios; normalization makes them probabilities
Connect outcomes, events, random variables, distributions, and conditioning
One observation can support several hidden causes
Bad traffic raises the construction belief from 0.5 to 0.75
Multiply a prior by a conditional to recover joint probability
Repeated product rules factor any joint distribution
Two factorizations of the same joint yield Bayes' rule
Posterior disease probability is not the probability that disease causes a symptom
Partition the hypothesis space, then add disjoint joint masses
A strong likelihood may still produce a small posterior when the prior is tiny
Dry conditions make sun much more probable than rain
The posterior combines prior belief, likelihood, and evidence prevalence
Including the prior makes the rule MAP, not maximum likelihood
The evidence normalizer combines all ways the observed purchase could occur
Represent uncertainty, compute an update, and defend the interpretation
